# Components

Source: https://openui.dev/docs/components

# Components

OpenUI components are source files, not a runtime library. Each one:

- uses only framework primitives and Tailwind CSS utilities;
- has **no OpenUI runtime dependency** and no third-party runtime dependency;
- ships a plain class-joining helper instead of `clsx` or `tailwind-merge`
  (variants are disjoint, so class conflicts do not arise);
- defaults to `type="button"` so a button inside a form never submits by
  accident.

## Button

The beta ships one reference component, `button`, implemented natively for all
four supported frameworks.

### Props

| Prop        | Type                                                         | Default   | Description                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `variant`   | `primary \| secondary \| outline \| ghost \| danger \| link` | `primary` | Visual emphasis.                       |
| `size`      | `sm \| md \| lg \| icon`                                     | `md`      | Control height and horizontal padding. |
| `fullWidth` | `boolean`                                                    | `false`   | Stretch to the container width.        |
| `type`      | `button \| submit \| reset`                                  | `button`  | Native button type.                    |
| `disabled`  | `boolean`                                                    | `false`   | Native disabled state.                 |

Every other native attribute (`aria-*`, `onClick`, `form`, …) is forwarded to
the underlying `<button>`.

### Variants

| Variant     | Use                                             |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `primary`   | The single highest-emphasis action on a screen. |
| `secondary` | Supporting action on a subtle surface.          |
| `outline`   | Bordered action in dense or neutral layouts.    |
| `ghost`     | Borderless action in toolbars.                  |
| `danger`    | Destructive or irreversible action.             |
| `link`      | Inline action styled like a link.               |

### Sizes

`sm` is 32px tall, `md` is 40px, `lg` is 48px, and `icon` is a 40×40 square.

### Accessibility

- Uses a real `<button>` element, so keyboard and screen-reader behavior is
  native.
- Includes a visible `focus-visible` ring with offset.
- Disabled buttons use both `disabled` and `pointer-events-none` plus reduced
  opacity.
- `type` defaults to `button` to avoid accidental form submission.
- For icon-only buttons, pass an accessible name:

```tsx
<Button size="icon" aria-label="Close dialog">
  <CloseIcon aria-hidden="true" />
</Button>
```

## Usage by framework

### React

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";

<Button variant="danger" size="lg" onClick={remove}>
  Delete project
</Button>;
```

### Svelte

```svelte
<script>
  import Button from "$lib/components/ui/button.svelte";
</script>

<Button variant="outline" size="sm" onclick={save}>Save</Button>
```

Svelte content is passed as a snippet:

```svelte
<Button>
  {#snippet children()}
    <span>Save</span>
  {/snippet}
</Button>
```

### Astro

```astro
---
import Button from "../components/ui/button.astro";
---

<Button variant="secondary" type="submit">Save</Button>
```

Astro content goes into the default slot.

### Vue

```vue
<script setup>
import Button from "@/components/ui/button.vue";
</script>

<template>
  <Button variant="ghost" @click="close">Close</Button>
</template>
```

Vue content goes into the default slot.

## Customizing

Components live in your project after installation. Edit them directly. Use
`openui diff button` to see what changed before pulling a registry update, and
`openui add button --overwrite` only when you intend to replace local edits.

Add new variants or sizes by editing the component's class maps. Keep variants
disjoint — for example, do not give two variants background utilities that can
conflict — so the simple join helper remains correct.
